accuracy.reason: All five objectives are correctly bounded: API implementation versus client/database, routing and validation, identity versus permission, acceptance versus completion and duplicate-safe retry responsibility. No universal database dependency or exactly-once claim.

evidence.quote: A known identity does not imply permission.

mechanisms.reason: Request routing/checks/handler/dependencies/response are traceable, as are queued acceptance, worker processing and terminal outcome. Lost acknowledgements explain duplicate effects. ApiServerDiagram matches optional storage and separate acceptance/result paths.

evidence.quote: a lost response or acknowledgement may hide an effect that already occurred.

coherence.reason: Program, network, HTTP and basic storage prerequisites are sufficient. Role precedes request processing, execution variants, coordination costs and the response-semantics design decision; all card objectives are taught.

evidence.quote: Choose the response promise before the execution path

decisions.reason: Immediate result requirements are compared with deferred waiting benefits and explicit queue/worker/status/retry costs. Invalid input, denied access and dependency failures must remain visible, preventing a default queue-for-everything prescription.

evidence.quote: Use deferred work when its waiting and workload benefits justify the extra queue, worker, status and duplicate-processing coordination.

clarity.reason: Defines middleware, authentication, authorization, queue, worker, idempotency and deduplication at useful introductory depth; concise parallel paths make acceptance distinct from success. Diagram/shared assets inspected, no UI execution claimed.

evidence.quote: An accepted request does not mean the work is complete.

outcomes.reason: Defines API and implementation boundary, client and storage responsibilities, optional database use and complete route/validate/authenticate/authorize/work/respond sequence. Explicitly denies authenticated-equals-authorized and prevents protected effects on failed checks.

Traces immediate outcome versus arranged deferred acceptance, queue/worker/job identity and pending/success/failure visibility. Identifies shorter acceptance wait without lower total work, extra operations/status and uncertain retry effects requiring deliberate idempotency/deduplication.

Selects immediate quick work versus justified long deferred work; connects checks and dependencies to accurate success/acceptance, visible errors or terminal job failure and extra deferred coordination. Correctly leaves exact status codes and rollback mechanics unspecified rather than inventing guarantees.

sourceChecks.claim: MDN distinguishes client presentation from server request processing and explicitly allows results from tools/communications instead of databases; supports API application work rather than storage equivalence.

OWASP requires per-endpoint access control, distinguishes authentication/authorization logic, validates format/type/range and rejects illegal content. These checks support prevention of disallowed effects.
Azure pattern documents accepted response, background work and status polling/resource completion as separate stages; acceptance is not finished work.

Azure explains client/background decoupling and extra complexity, status outcomes and idempotency keys returning existing jobs after uncertain POST retries. AWS idempotent API guidance checked earlier additionally supports avoiding repeated side effects.

Azure pattern selection and status contract support deferral when needed and visible terminal results; checked OWASP input/access requirements apply before protected work. It does not promise automatic performance or duplicate prevention.
